From 581073f626e387d3e7eed55c48c8495584ead7ba Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2024 16:33:58 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] af_packet: do not call packet_read_pending() from
 tpacket_destruct_skb()

trafgen performance considerably sank on hosts with many cores
after the blamed commit.

packet_read_pending() is very expensive, and calling it
in af_packet fast path defeats Daniel intent in commit
b013840810c2 ("packet: use percpu mmap tx frame pending refcount")

tpacket_destruct_skb() makes room for one packet, we can immediately
wakeup a producer, no need to completely drain the tx ring.

Fixes: 89ed5b519004 ("af_packet: Block execution of tasks waiting for transmit to complete in AF_PACKET")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Neil Horman <nhorman@tuxdriver.com>
Cc: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Reviewed-by: Willem de Bruijn <willemb@google.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240515163358.4105915-1-edumazet@google.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/packet/af_packet.c b/net/packet/af_packet.c
index 8c6d3fbb4ed8..ea3ebc160e25 100644
--- a/net/packet/af_packet.c
+++ b/net/packet/af_packet.c
@@ -2522,8 +2522,7 @@ static void tpacket_destruct_skb(struct sk_buff *skb)
 		ts = __packet_set_timestamp(po, ph, skb);
 		__packet_set_status(po, ph, TP_STATUS_AVAILABLE | ts);
 
-		if (!packet_read_pending(&po->tx_ring))
-			complete(&po->skb_completion);
+		complete(&po->skb_completion);
 	}
 
 	sock_wfree(skb);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/packet/af_packet.c`**
- The function `tpacket_destruct_skb()` was modified to remove the call to `packet_read_pending(&po->tx_ring)`. 
- The line that checks if there are pending packets and conditionally calls `complete(&po->skb_completion)` was replaced with a direct call to `complete(&po->skb_completion)` without the condition.

### Relationships
- The modification aims to improve performance by eliminating the expensive call to `packet_read_pending()` in the fast path of the `tpacket_destruct_skb()` function. 
- This change is intended to address performance issues observed in `trafgen` on multi-core hosts, which arose after a previous commit that introduced blocking behavior for tasks waiting on transmit completion. 
- The patch effectively simplifies the logic in `tpacket_destruct_skb()` by ensuring that the completion of the socket buffer is always signaled, thereby allowing for immediate wakeup of the producer without needing to check for pending packets.

Here is the commit message:
af_packet: do not call packet_read_pending() from
 tpacket_destruct_skb()

trafgen performance considerably sank on hosts with many cores
after the blamed commit.

packet_read_pending() is very expensive, and calling it
in af_packet fast path defeats Daniel intent in commit
b013840810c2 ("packet: use percpu mmap tx frame pending refcount")

tpacket_destruct_skb() makes room for one packet, we can immediately
wakeup a producer, no need to completely drain the tx ring.

Fixes: 89ed5b519004 ("af_packet: Block execution of tasks waiting for transmit to complete in AF_PACKET")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Neil Horman <nhorman@tuxdriver.com>
Cc: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>
Reviewed-by: Willem de Bruijn <willemb@google.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240515163358.4105915-1-edumazet@google.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug was the introduction of a call to `packet_read_pending()` within the `tpacket_destruct_skb()` function, which is part of the AF_PACKET implementation. This call was expensive and negatively impacted performance, particularly on hosts with many cores, as it added unnecessary overhead in the fast path of packet processing. The intent of the previous commit was to block execution of tasks waiting for transmit to complete, but this led to a significant performance degradation in scenarios where quick packet processing was essential.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void tpacket_destruct_skb(struct sk_buff *skb)
 {
 	struct packet_sock *po = pkt_sk(skb->sk);
 
 	if (likely(po->tx_ring.pg_vec)) {
 		void *ph;
 		__u32 ts;
 
 		ph = skb_zcopy_get_nouarg(skb);
 		packet_dec_pending(&po->tx_ring);
 
 		ts = __packet_set_timestamp(po, ph, skb);
 		__packet_set_status(po, ph, TP_STATUS_AVAILABLE | ts);
 
-		if (!packet_read_pending(&po->tx_ring))
-			complete(&po->skb_completion);
+		complete(&po->skb_completion);
 	}
 
 	sock_wfree(skb);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (!packet_read_pending(&po->tx_ring))
    complete(&po->skb_completion);
```
Reason:
The call to `packet_read_pending()` is expensive and was introduced in the `tpacket_destruct_skb()` function, which is part of the fast path for packet processing. This unnecessary overhead significantly degraded performance, especially on multi-core hosts, as it added latency to the packet handling process.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
complete(&po->skb_completion);
```
Reason:
By removing the call to `packet_read_pending()` and directly calling `complete(&po->skb_completion);`, the patch eliminates the performance overhead while still allowing the completion of the skb processing. This change restores the intended fast path behavior for packet processing without the unnecessary delay introduced by the pending check.
